ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.method: Two independent sweeps. (1) A FIXED-STRING tracked-file sweep with git grep -F over the whole worktree for each candidate literal, counting occurrences per file. (2) An EXHAUSTIVE REF sweep: for every ref returned by git for-each-ref, git ls-tree -r --name-only was run and filtered for the candidate paths, so that a collision hiding on a branch this worktree has never checked out would still be found.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_two_sweeps_are_both_needed: The tracked-file sweep sees CONTENT at this head but not other branches. The ref sweep sees PATHS on every branch but not content. A candidate that is textually absent here yet materialized on a sibling branch is invisible to the first and caught by the second, which is exactly the shape a competing lane's allocation would take.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_FIXED_STRING_and_not_regex: git grep -F treats the pattern as a literal. The candidate ids contain '.' characters which a regex would treat as wildcards, so a regex sweep could match v1.0.35 against a hypothetical v1x0y35 and report a false collision, or - worse for a negative claim - be quietly miscounted.
